title: Show each monitor's own workspaces in the bar

decision: findings: global bound switch drops unbound 1-5 placeholders; disabled rules counted; marker scope; dropped refresh; overlapping PRs

leads.summary: Disabled workspace rules still activate per-monitor mode in the bar
leads.consequence: A configured hl.workspace_rule({workspace='2', monitor='DP-1', enabled=false}) does not bind workspace 2 in Hyprland, but the widget treats it as binding. If it is the only monitor rule, the bar switches from its default 1-5 list to the disabled rule's [2] (plus currently live workspaces).
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F5 disabled rules); corroboration; published

leads.summary: Valid Hyprland desc: selectors can silently disappear from the bar's rule map
leads.consequence: For example, monitor='desc: Dell Inc.' is resolved by Hyprland after trimming the space but ignored by the widget. Additionally a desc: prefix that extends into text present only in the full hardware description, not the shortened monitors -j description, can resolve in Hyprland but fail in the widget. If no other monitor rule is recognized, each bar falls back to the global 1-5 list; if other rules exist the skipped monitor has only existing workspaces, not its as-yet-uncreated bound slots.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F5 desc: trim/full description); corroboration; published as minor note

leads.summary: A second rules-change event received during a rules query is discarded
leads.consequence: If a config reload or monitor change follows a first query while its Process remains running and that query sees the old state, the second notification does not cause a new query. The bar retains the old bound workspace list until a later relevant event or shell restart. The paired monitoradded/monitoraddedv2 notifications also pass through this gate, so repeated notifications are not a dependable retry.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3 dropped refresh); corroboration; published

leads.summary: Open PR #12659 independently adds the same WorkspacesModel.js with incompatible exports
leads.consequence: Both PRs add WorkspacesModel.js at the same path with different content. Merging one onto the other requires a manual combined model: keeping #13369's model makes #12659's tests fail on missing baseOpacity/shouldFlash, while keeping #12659's model makes this PR's workspaces-test.sh fail on missing monitorRuleIds/workspaceIds and leaves this QML broken. The QML edits also overlap.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified with read-only gh (#12659 open, adds WorkspacesModel.js with baseOpacity/shouldFlash); Opus confirmed in self-check; published

leads.summary: Other open workspace-widget PRs #12978 and #9094 require explicit conflict resolution
leads.consequence: The two PRs edit overlapping Workspaces.qml hunks and cannot be applied as-is. If the merged widget preserves this PR's per-monitor rule parser/list while adopting #12978's global mode, the later monitor's raw IDs (for example 12 on monitor 2) are excluded by the <=10 test, so its slots/active workspace can disappear; if it instead adopts #12978's workspaceIds/slotOfId, this PR's rule-based per-monitor display is replaced. A combined implementation must convert workspace IDs to per-monitor logical slots consistently and route clicks through the global-mode command. Independently, #9094 changes the same QML list, click and marker lines to support named IDs beyond 10, and its workspaces-widget-test.sh requires the uncapped list and on_current_monitor click. If #9094's tests are retained with this PR's widget, the tests fail, including the checks for the uncapped list implementation in QML and the click command. #12997 also edits the focused marker line, so its unfocused-monitor opacity choice should be reconciled explicitly.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #12978/#9094/#12997 open and touching Workspaces.qml; Opus confirmed #12978 IDs >10 in self-check; published as overlap list

leads.summary: A workspace with no monitor association is omitted instead of shown on its active bar
leads.consequence: In per-monitor mode, if Quickshell knows a workspace ID but its monitor pointer is temporarily absent and that workspace has no explicit rule on this bar, its button is hidden entirely, including the indicator for the workspace currently displayed there. This is most relevant while monitor/workspace IPC state is being rebuilt during hotplug; whether it persists on a particular compositor setup has not been measured.
leads.triage: hypothesis (null workspace.monitor during teardown hides live ID); needs desktop; unconfirmed, dropped

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified by source and model runs:** for the setup this PR targets, where every relevant workspace is bound to a monitor by connector or `desc:` rules such as hyprmoncfg writes, each bar lists its own workspaces. Without any monitor-bound rules, the list is unchanged from the current widget. The main issue is a mixed setup: a single numbered rule for a connected monitor switches every bar into per-monitor mode, and unbound workspaces 1-5 that do not exist yet then disappear from all bars.

### A single monitor-bound rule removes the unbound 1-5 placeholders from every bar

`bound` in `WorkspacesModel.js:54` is global. As soon as any connected monitor has a numbered rule, every bar stops starting from `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` (`:64-72`) and lists only its own rule IDs plus workspaces that already live on its monitor (`:77`). Unbound IDs that do not exist yet are then shown on no bar.

Model run with a laptop (`eDP-1`) and a TV (`HDMI-A-1`), a single rule pinning workspace 10 to the TV, and existing workspaces 1 (laptop) and 10 (TV). The widget labels workspace 10 as `0`:

```text
                current widget      this PR
laptop bar      1 2 3 4 5 0         1
TV bar          1 2 3 4 5 0         0
```

**Impact:** partial rule sets lose their empty workspace buttons. Omarchy's manual suggests binding specific workspaces to monitors (`manual/33-monitors.md:41`), so partial sets are a documented setup. The PR's own test expects a monitor without rules to show only the workspaces living on it, so that part looks intended; losing 2-5 on every bar probably does not. hyprmoncfg's default plans bind 1-9, so the PR's target setup is not affected.

**Suggested change:** keep the default IDs 1-5 on a bar unless a rule binds that ID to another connected monitor or the workspace currently lives on another monitor.

### Disabled rules still count as bindings

`hyprctl workspacerules -j` prints every rule with an `enabled` field, and Hyprland ignores disabled rules when it decides which monitor a workspace belongs to (`WorkspaceRuleManager.cpp`, Hyprland 0.56.2). `monitorRuleIds()` never reads `enabled`. In a model run, a rule for workspace 6 on `DP-3` with `"enabled": false` gives `{"DP-3": [6]}`, where Hyprland binds nothing.

**Impact:** because of the global switch above, one disabled rule is enough to put every bar into per-monitor mode, although Hyprland does not apply that rule.

**Suggested change:** skip the rule in `monitorRuleIds()` with `if (rule.enabled === false) return`.

**Minor selector differences:** Hyprland trims the text after `desc:` and matches it as a prefix of the full output description, which ends in ` (<connector>)`. `hyprctl monitors -j` only prints the short description. A `desc:` selector with trailing whitespace, or one written against the full description, binds in Hyprland but not in the model. hyprmoncfg's selectors match correctly.

### The per-monitor marker also applies without rules

The PR lists the per-monitor marker as its own change. It is not limited to setups with rules: head `Workspaces.qml:99-101` marks each monitor's own active workspace whenever the bar's monitor resolves. On two monitors without rules, both bars list the same IDs but mark different ones, so the widget no longer shows which workspace has keyboard focus. On a single monitor the marker is equivalent to the current one.

**Impact:** on multi-monitor setups without rules, the bar loses its indication of which workspace has keyboard focus. The change may well be wanted: open PRs #8435, #11976 and draft #12997 propose the same marker, and #12997 also adds a keyboard-focus indicator.

**Suggested change:** state in the PR description that the marker change reaches all multi-monitor setups, not only those with rules.

### A rules refresh requested during a running query is dropped

`reloadRules()` does nothing while `rulesProcess` is running (`Workspaces.qml:44-46`), and nothing re-runs it afterwards. `KeyboardLayout.qml` in the same directory already handles the same case with `refreshPending` (lines 43-53 and 133).

**Impact:** if a second `configreloaded` or monitor event arrives during a query that already read the older state, the bar keeps stale rules until the next such event. No common sequence that triggers this was found.

**Suggested change:** reuse that pattern: set a pending flag when a refresh is requested while the process runs, and re-run it once the process finishes if the flag is set.

**Other behaviour changes:** a single monitor with 1-9 bound to it shows 9 buttons instead of 5, and, when monitor-bound rules exist, a monitor with no rules of its own whose only workspaces are above 10 shows an empty widget.

### Overlapping open PRs

- #12659 ("Flash workspace buttons when they need attention") also adds `shell/plugins/bar/widgets/WorkspacesModel.js`, with different exports (`baseOpacity`, `shouldFlash`). Whichever PR merges second needs a combined file.
- #9094, #10639 and #12978 change the same list or click logic in `Workspaces.qml`. #12978 uses workspace IDs above 10 on the second monitor, which this model drops.

**Verified:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/shell.d/workspaces-test.sh` and `plugins-test.sh` at head | pass |
| Four behavioural mutations of `WorkspacesModel.js` (moved-away filter, monitor filter, exact `desc:` match, no `desc:` branch) | each fails the PR test; an unchanged copy passes |
| List without rules, or with rules but an unresolved bar monitor, compared with the current widget's `workspaceIds()` | identical in 6000 of 6000 randomized cases (3000 of each) |
| The QML's `sh -c` command against a stub `hyprctl` | produces valid JSON; `%` and quotes in descriptions pass through; on `hyprctl` failure the previous rules are kept |
| `omarchy-plugin-clone omarchy.workspaces` | clone includes a byte-identical `WorkspacesModel.js` |
| Field names and events | match Hyprland 0.56.2 (`workspaceString`, `monitor`, `name`, `description`; `configreloaded`, `monitoradded*`, `monitorremoved*`) |

**Test scope:** source review of the PR at `69d5c7d` against Hyprland 0.56.2 source, Quickshell `28771c7` (the commit Omarchy's package repository pins), and hyprmoncfg at its current default branch. The PR's test, the plugin test, mutation checks, randomized comparisons of the pure model, the shell command with a stub `hyprctl`, and the plugin clone ran in an isolated sandbox. Nothing ran against a live compositor: the QML event handling, marker and hotplug timing were assessed from source only, and the author's two-monitor check is the only runtime evidence for them.
